account: In July 2022 a previously healthy woman in her early 40s was admitted to Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center, Israel. She had a month of worsening headaches. Imaging showed a 2.6 cm left apical lung adenocarcinoma with leptomeningeal spread, and biopsy tissue was scarce. To guide gene testing without exhausting tissue, the team ran Imagene's deep-learning algorithm on the slide stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). Within 48 hours of biopsy it inferred that the tumor was positive for a mutation in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene. A rapid Idylla polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay confirmed the L858R exon 21 mutation, and osimertinib started two days after biopsy. The authors say that this was one week earlier than routine practice and avoided whole-neuraxis radiotherapy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at two months showed the enhancement gone. In February 2023 a second woman in her early 40s with EGFR-mutant lung cancer at the same center followed the same path, and her MRI also improved at two months. The case report was first published online on 18 July 2023. In January 2026 Imagene staff and partner pathologists reported that the company's later EGFR classifier reached an area under the curve of 0.87 on 968 slides from two centers. Of the slides that it called likely positive for EGFR, 79.3% carried the mutation on conventional testing.

ai_role.statement: The AI inference directed which rapid test to run; treatment began only after PCR confirmation. The AI therefore changed the sequence and speed of testing rather than the final diagnosis. Authors are Tel Aviv Sourasky / Tel Aviv University clinicians declaring no competing interests. A second patient in the report (February 2023) followed the same path.

The authors say that this was one week earlier than routine practice and avoided whole-neuraxis radiotherapy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at two months showed the enhancement gone. In February 2023 a second woman in her early 40s with EGFR-mutant lung cancer at the same center followed the same path, and her MRI also improved at two months. The case report was first published online on 18 July 2023. In January 2026 Imagene staff and partner pathologists reported that the company's later EGFR classifier reached an area under the curve of 0.87 on 968 slides from two centers. Of the slides that it called likely positive for EGFR, 79.3% carried the mutation on conventional testing.
